items.primary_i_can: I can distinguish between “no forces acting” and “no net force acting.” and identify support force, weight, and other common forces in simple situations.
items.evidence_job: Navigate a connected force-and-motion stimulus by isolating the object, identifying forces, reading motion evidence, and planning a Newton’s First Law explanation.
items.source_basis: Original Unit 1 Assessment Plan §1.2: Newton’s First Law, inertia, zero-net-force distinction, support force/weight; Physics Framework: physical-situation force reasoning.
items.student_text:
A rolling equipment cart moves to the right at a steady speed across a level hallway. Its force model is:

            180 N support ↑
  35 N ←      [cart]      → 35 N
            180 N weight ↓

(a) Identify the object being modeled and list the forces acting on it.
(b) Determine the horizontal and vertical net force.
(c) Explain why ‘forces are acting’ and ‘net force is zero’ can both be true.
(d) Use Newton’s First Law to predict the cart’s motion if the force model remains unchanged.
items.student_html:
A rolling equipment cart moves to the right at a steady speed across a level hallway. Its force model is:

180 N support ↑
35 N ← [cart] → 35 N
180 N weight ↓

(a) Identify the object being modeled and list the forces acting on it.
(b) Determine the horizontal and vertical net force.
(c) Explain why ‘forces are acting’ and ‘net force is zero’ can both be true.
(d) Use Newton’s First Law to predict the cart’s motion if the force model remains unchanged.
items.answer: (a) The cart; support up, weight down, a 35 N leftward force, and a 35 N rightward force. (b) 0 N horizontally and 0 N vertically. (c) Opposing forces can cancel even though each force is real. (d) It continues with constant velocity: steady speed in a straight line.
items.solution_text: The diagram isolates one object. Equal opposite forces cancel on each axis, so ΣF = 0. Newton’s First Law says zero net force means the cart’s velocity does not change.
items.solution_html: The diagram isolates one object. Equal opposite forces cancel on each axis, so ΣF = 0. Newton’s First Law says zero net force means the cart’s velocity does not change.

items.student_text: A hockey puck glides across nearly frictionless ice with zero net force. Predict its motion and state Newton’s First Law in everyday language.
items.student_html: A hockey puck glides across nearly frictionless ice with zero net force. Predict its motion and state Newton’s First Law in everyday language.
items.answer: It keeps moving in a straight line at constant speed; motion changes only when a nonzero net force acts.
items.solution_text: Zero net force means zero change in velocity. Newton’s First Law says an object keeps its state of rest or constant straight-line motion unless a net force changes it.
items.solution_html: Zero net force means zero change in velocity. Newton’s First Law says an object keeps its state of rest or constant straight-line motion unless a net force changes it.

items.student_text: A space probe coasts far from strong interactions. Its net force is zero. What happens to its velocity? Explain with Newton’s First Law.
items.student_html: A space probe coasts far from strong interactions. Its net force is zero. What happens to its velocity? Explain with Newton’s First Law.
items.solution_text: With no net force, there is no reason for the velocity to change; it continues at the same speed and direction.

items.student_text: A student says, ‘When a bus stops, passengers lurch forward because an inertia force pushes them forward.’ Critique the statement and replace it with a correct explanation.
items.student_html: A student says, ‘When a bus stops, passengers lurch forward because an inertia force pushes them forward.’ Critique the statement and replace it with a correct explanation.
items.answer: There is no inertia force; inertia is the property of matter that resists changes in velocity, so passengers tend to keep moving forward while the bus slows.
items.solution_text: Inertia is not an interaction force. The passenger’s body tends to maintain its previous motion until actual forces from the seat, belt, or floor change it.
items.solution_html: Inertia is not an interaction force. The passenger’s body tends to maintain its previous motion until actual forces from the seat, belt, or floor change it.

items.student_text: A student says, ‘A book resists being pushed because inertia pulls backward on it.’ Correct the explanation.
items.student_html: A student says, ‘A book resists being pushed because inertia pulls backward on it.’ Correct the explanation.
items.answer: Inertia does not pull backward; it is the book’s tendency to resist a change in motion because it has mass.
items.solution_text: A backward arrow labeled inertia would be a fake force. Inertia describes resistance to changing velocity, not an interaction.
items.solution_html: A backward arrow labeled inertia would be a fake force. Inertia describes resistance to changing velocity, not an interaction.

items.student_text: A 20 N book rests on a level table. Draw a force diagram for the book only. Label each force and explain why the diagram can contain forces even though the book is not accelerating.
items.student_html: A 20 N book rests on a level table. Draw a force diagram for the book only. Label each force and explain why the diagram can contain forces even though the book is not accelerating.
items.answer: Draw 20 N weight downward and 20 N support force upward; the forces are real but balance to zero net force.
items.solution_text: The Earth pulls down on the book and the table pushes up. Equal opposite forces cancel, so the book has zero net force without having ‘no forces.’
items.solution_html: The Earth pulls down on the book and the table pushes up. Equal opposite forces cancel, so the book has zero net force without having ‘no forces.’

items.student_text: A hanging sign weighs 90 N and is motionless on a vertical cable. Draw a force diagram for the sign only and label the forces.
items.student_html: A hanging sign weighs 90 N and is motionless on a vertical cable. Draw a force diagram for the sign only and label the forces.
items.answer: Draw 90 N weight downward and 90 N cable tension upward.
items.solution_text: The sign is the object of interest. Earth’s weight force points down and the cable’s tension points up. Because it is motionless, these forces balance.

items.student_text: Force model: 50 N ← [crate] → 50 N. Motion description: the crate moves right at a steady 1.5 m/s. Can the model and motion description represent the same situation? Explain.
items.student_html: Force model: 50 N ← [crate] → 50 N. Motion description: the crate moves right at a steady 1.5 m/s. Can the model and motion description represent the same situation? Explain.
items.answer: Yes; the horizontal forces balance, so net force is zero and constant rightward velocity is possible.
items.solution_text: Balanced forces do not imply zero velocity. They imply no change in velocity, which is consistent with steady straight-line motion.
items.solution_html: Balanced forces do not imply zero velocity. They imply no change in velocity, which is consistent with steady straight-line motion.

items.student_text: Force model: 12 N ← [cart] → 12 N. Motion description: the cart is speeding up to the right. Are the two descriptions consistent? Explain.
items.student_html: Force model: 12 N ← [cart] → 12 N. Motion description: the cart is speeding up to the right. Are the two descriptions consistent? Explain.
items.answer: No; the balanced model gives zero net force, so it cannot account for a change in velocity.
items.solution_text: A cart speeding up requires nonzero net force in the direction of the velocity change. The shown forces cancel.
items.solution_html: A cart speeding up requires nonzero net force in the direction of the velocity change. The shown forces cancel.
